about: Per-part syllabus tags for AA HL. Each part was tagged by two independent blind reviewers against data/syllabus.json and data/syllabus-aa-hl.json; parts where they disagreed were settled by an adjudicator (review: adjudicated, with rationale and both original tag sets). HL appearances of SL questions (data/shared.json) take the SL tags and are not listed here.

parts.label: b
parts.skill: Use the sum of roots to find an unknown coefficient of a quartic

parts.label: b

parts.rationale: Both marks come from setting the gradient to zero to locate stationary points, which is the 5.8 idea; the differential equation only supplies the gradient expression and is not solved here, so 5.18 is secondary.

parts.label: b

parts.rationale: Five of the seven marks are for solving f'(x)=0 and giving the stationary-point coordinates (5.8), with two for the chain-rule derivative of squared trig terms (5.6); solving sin 2x = 0 is a single routine mark inside the 5.8 work, so 3.8 is not added.

parts.label: b
parts.skill: Prove the arctan addition formula with the tan compound angle identity and apply it to the argument of a product
parts.rationale: Part (i) is earned by the tan compound angle identity (3.10), and part (ii) by adding arguments of a product in polar terms (1.13) before applying the arctan result, so 1.13 carries more marks than the inverse-trig notation of 3.9.

parts.label: c
parts.skill: Prove by induction a formula for the argument of a product of complex numbers using the arctan addition result

parts.label: b
parts.skill: Find the median of a continuous random variable by setting the integral to one half and solving with technology
parts.rationale: The marks are for setting the cumulative integral of the pdf to one half and solving for the median, which 4.14 names directly; the technology solve is incidental and does not need 2.10.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.skill: Find the exact limit of the angle between vectors as n tends to infinity
Find a rate of change of height from a volume rate using related rates, solving a cubic for h with technology
parts.rationale: Most marks are for linking dh/dt to dV/dt through the chain rule (5.14 related rates), and a separate independent M1A1 is for solving the cubic V=200 for h on the GDC, a technology solve that 2.10 covers.

parts.label: a

parts.rationale: Three marks come from the cosine rule in each triangle (3.2), and the final mark needs the angle expressed with arccos, which is inverse trig as a function under 3.9.

parts.label: b

parts.rationale: The marks are for setting the tangent gradient equal to 1 and finding the point, which 5.4 covers as where a tangent has a given gradient; the GDC solve is just the way to finish, not the assessed skill, so 2.10 is not added.

parts.label: a
parts.skill: Evaluate a given definite integral for a cone's curved surface area with specific values
parts.rationale: Both marks come from evaluating a definite integral exactly by hand, which the 5.11 tagWhen names, rather than the indefinite integration of 5.5.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.skill: Deduce the radius of a cone formed by rotating a line segment

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.skill: Deduce the slant height of the cone in terms of the parameters

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.skill: Evaluate the general surface area integral to derive the cone curved surface area formula
parts.rationale: All three marks are for evaluating the general definite integral and rewriting it in terms of r and l (5.11); the cone formula is the target, but no 3.1 solid-geometry work earns marks.

parts.label: c
parts.skill: Differentiate a square root function using the chain rule

parts.label: d
parts.skill: Substitute into a surface area integral and simplify to derive the surface area of a sphere
parts.rationale: The marks are for substituting y and dy/dx into the surface-area integral, simplifying, and evaluating it by hand between -r and r (5.11); the derivative was found in (c), so 5.6 is not new content here.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.skill: Describe the horizontal stretch given by y = f(kx)

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.skill: State the x-intercepts of a horizontally stretched graph
parts.rationale: The single mark comes from applying the horizontal stretch to the original intercepts at plus and minus r, which is a 2.11 transformation; nothing is read from a graph or GDC, so 2.4 is not added.

parts.label: e(iii)
parts.skill: Differentiate the transformed square root function with the chain rule

parts.label: e(iv)
parts.skill: Form and simplify a definite integral with correct limits for the surface area of an ellipsoid
parts.rationale: The marks are for substituting into the integral, simplifying the integrand to a polynomial under the root, and setting correct limits, all 5.11 definite-integral work; the derivative comes from (iii), so 5.6 is not re-tagged.

parts.label: e(v)
parts.skill: Choose model parameters and evaluate a surface area integral with technology, giving the answer in standard form

parts.label: a
parts.skill: Evaluate the next term of a population recurrence with growth and removal
parts.rationale: The marks are for applying the growth-and-removal recurrence once; this is a population model, not money, so 1.3 applies rather than 1.4, which the tagWhen keeps for financial contexts.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.skill: Verify a further term of the recurrence
parts.rationale: One mark is for iterating the population recurrence again; the context is not financial, so 1.3 is used rather than 1.4.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.skill: Compute a later term of the recurrence
parts.rationale: The marks are for one more iteration of the recurrence; with a population rather than money context, 1.3 is used instead of 1.4.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.skill: Simplify a closed form containing a geometric series sum

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.skill: Evaluate a term from the closed-form geometric model
parts.rationale: The marks are for evaluating a term from the closed form that contains a geometric term (1.3); the finance-solver route is only an alternative method, and the trout context is not financial, so 1.4 is not used.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.skill: Show the difference of consecutive terms of the closed form is a geometric expression
parts.rationale: The marks come from manipulating integer powers of 1.1 to simplify the difference of consecutive terms (1.5), with the geometric-sequence closed form (1.3) as the setting.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.skill: Use the sign of the consecutive difference to deduce the sequence is decreasing
parts.rationale: The reasoning mark is for using the sign of the consecutive-term difference to conclude that the sequence decreases, a property of the sequence model (1.3); no exponent manipulation earns this mark, so 1.5 does not fit.

parts.label: e
parts.skill: Find the first n for which the model becomes non-positive using logarithms or tabulation
parts.rationale: The main method solves the exponential inequality with logarithms or change of base (1.7), and the equally valid route of evaluating terms either side of zero makes the sequence (1.3) secondary.

parts.label: f
parts.skill: Find the removal amount that keeps the modelled population constant

parts.label: g
parts.skill: Prove by induction the closed form of a first-order linear recurrence

parts.label: a(i)
parts.skill: Solve a quadratic giving exact surd roots

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.skill: Show two surd roots are reciprocals via their product or rationalising

parts.label: b
parts.skill: Show the imaginary roots of x^2 + 1 = 0 are reciprocals using complex arithmetic
parts.rationale: The marks come from Cartesian complex arithmetic showing that the reciprocal of i is -i, or that the product of the roots is 1 (1.12); finding the roots of x^2+1=0 is immediate, so 2.7 earns nothing.

parts.label: c
parts.skill: Verify algebraically a general identity linking p(x) and p(1/x) for a palindromic quadratic
parts.rationale: The marks are for algebraically verifying an identity that holds for all a, b and nonzero x, which is proving a general identity under 1.6 rather than a numerical show-that; it uses no factor or remainder theorem, so 2.12 does not apply.

parts.label: d
parts.skill: Prove that the reciprocal of a nonzero root of a palindromic polynomial is also a root
parts.rationale: The A1 and R1 are for a deductive argument that a general statement about roots holds (1.6), and the statement concerns zeros of a polynomial of any degree (2.12), which is the secondary tag.

parts.label: e
parts.skill: Prove that the product of two palindromic polynomials is palindromic

parts.label: f
parts.skill: Equate coefficients of a quartic and its quadratic factorisation and solve for the unknowns
parts.rationale: Expanding the quadratic factors and equating coefficients to find unknown coefficients is 2.12, and solving the resulting system reduces to a quadratic in u or v, which earns its own M1A1 under 2.7.

parts.label: g
parts.skill: Solve the quadratic factors to find exact real and complex roots of a quartic

parts.label: h
parts.skill: Prove -1 is always a root of an odd-degree palindromic polynomial using the factor theorem
